Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Electron should respect the system trust store so that Auth0 API calls succeed when the enterprise root CA (e.g., Zscaler) is installed in the OS trust store.


### Actual Behavior

But API calls fail behind corporate firewall Zscaler with the error:

`unable to get local issuer certificate
`

On personal laptops (no firewall), the same calls succeed.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information
Which trust store does Electron/Chromium use, and how can we ensure it always uses the system trust store?


_No response_

nodes.title: Passing preload option in window.open in the renderer process
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS 15.6.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

According to the [documentation](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/window-open) (shown below), `window.open` allows a subset of web preferences options, including `preload`. That said, calling `window.open("google.com", "_blank", "contextIsolation=no,preload=/path/to/preload.js")` should be able to open a window with the preload script executed when there is no hook defined in the main process.

> A subset of [WebPreferences](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/structures/web-preferences) can be set directly, unnested, from the features string: zoomFactor, nodeIntegration, preload, javascript, contextIsolation, and webviewTag

### Actual Behavior

Calling `window.open("google.com", "_blank", "contextIsolation=no,preload=/path/to/preload.js")` in a window without any main-process hook cannot load the specified preload script in the new window.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/jackfromeast/9aec442ad011668c4597f31852cef2da

Put all the files under a folder and run:

```
npm install && npm start
```

### Additional Information

Hi, I’m wondering whether this is an intended behavior and the documentation should be updated, or if it’s unexpected and needs to be fixed. Thank you!

nodes.title: Accessibility: Hidden windows present themselves as active to Linux screenreaders
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

openSUSE Tumbleweed 20250904

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When calling the .hide() method on a BrowserWindow instance, the window disappears from the screen, and should also fire a window deactivate accessibility event to screenreaders through at-spi. When queried for its state by a running screenreader, the window should report itself as inactive until it's shown again. These mechanisms allow the screenreaders to determine which window is currently focused, and provide the user with appropriate feedback and various navigation tools.

### Actual Behavior

After calling the .hide() method, the window disappears, but the deactivation a11y event is not fired and when queried by the assistive tech, the window presents itself as active despite it's hidden.

This is a quite severe problem for Linux screenreaders. The user may be running various popular Electron apps like Signal, Element or Discord in the background, but these all report themselves as active to the screenreader, which afterwards often reads a completely different window to the user from the one they actually want to use, because it's unable to determine which of them is really focused.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/RastislavKish/c9ec92351be7c9e77d965e601465f4c9

### Additional Information

Reproduction steps

Detecting the status of windows with a screenreader directly is complicated, because Orca, the Linux screenreader, applies some mitigations against this problem, and so the results can be somewhat unpredictable. But there is an official Orca script which prints plain at-spi window activations and deactivations to the terminal, as well as a list of windows claiming to be active. This python script only requires at-spi2-core-dev libraries and the gobject introspection libraries, which are both included in the repositories of all common Linux distributions.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Clone the official Orca repository and cd into the tools directory:

```sh
git clone https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/orca.git
cd orca/tools
```

2. Turn on Orca, so we can be sure the Electron a11y stack starts properly.
3. Start Electron fiddle, and load the attached gist. This gist is the standard hello world app, which after 5 seconds upon launch calls mainWindow.hide()
4. Return to the terminal, and launch:

```sh
python3 dump-window-events.py
```

5. Switch the window, either by mouse or by using Alt+Tab, back to the Electron fiddle and hit F5 to run the gist.
6. Wait until the Hello world app launches, stays for 5 seconds and disappears.
7. Switch the window, either by mouse or pressing Alt+Tab, back to the terminal with the running script. The script should notice the terminal has been focused and exit automatically. Check the output.

In the output, you should see the Hello world app fires the activation event when it first appears on the screen, but then does not fire the deactivation event when it hides, and when switching windows, it keeps reporting itself as being active, even though only one window should always be active at once.

I'm attaching the output of the command captured on my machine running GNOME 48.4 Wayland. Ignore everything from mutter-x11-frames, what matters for Orca are the events from the real apps.

Note: If you don't see *any* accessibility events from the electron apps, i.e. electron-fiddle and the Hello world app, it may be necessary to set the ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED environment variable to 1, and if it doesn't help, also use --force-renderer-accessibility flag with the Hello world app. Neither of these should be necessary by default when Orca is turned on, but there are certain setups where the AT auto-detection mechanism fails for various reasons.

[dump-window-events-output.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22191937/dump-window-events-output.log)

nodes.title: navigationHistory corrupted when navigating forward to pages containing iframes in WebContentsView
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Sequoia 15.6.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When using goForward() to navigate to any page, navigationHistory.canGoBack() and canGoForward() should maintain accurate state regardless of page content.

### Actual Behavior

When using goForward() to navigate to a page containing iframes, the navigationHistory gets corrupted:

- History length suddenly decreases
- canGoBack() and canGoForward() return false when they should return true
- Navigation state becomes inconsistent

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

#### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a WebContentsView with navigationHistory tracking
2. Navigate through several pages to build up history (e.g., 6+ entries)
3. Use goBack() multiple times to go to earlier pages
4. Use goForward() to navigate to a page that contains iframes
5. Observe that navigationHistory suddenly becomes corrupted

#### Code Example
```typescript
// Navigation event tracking
webContentsView.webContents.on("did-navigate-in-page", (_, navigationUrl, isMainFrame) => {
  if (isMainFrame) {
    const history = tab.webContentsView.webContents.navigationHistory;
    console.log(
      `🟡 AFTER did-navigate-in-page: ${history.canGoBack()}/${history.canGoForward()} == ${history.getActiveIndex()}/${history.length()}`
    );
  }
});

// goForward
webContentsView.webContents.navigationHistory.goForward();
```

#### console output
```text
// Normal navigation - working correctly
🟡 AFTER did-navigate-in-page: true/true == 2/11

// goForward() to page with iframe - navigationHistory corrupted
🟡 AFTER did-navigate-in-page: false/false == 3/4  ← History corrupted: length changed from 11 to 4
```

Accelerators such as `CmdOrCtrl+B` do not work while `contenteditable` elements are focused
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.2.5

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 15.6.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Sort of. This is presumably an intentional behaviour of Chromium to prevent browser keyboard shortcuts from colliding with the default `contenteditable` shortcuts. However, this behaviour is unlikely to be useful in Electron. If the developer defines an accelerator, it should take precedence over Chromium's default behaviour.

### Expected Behavior

1. The developer defines an accelerator for `CmdOrCtrl+B` in the application menu
2. The user focuses a `contenteditable` element inside the Electron app
3. The user presses `command+b` or `ctrl+b`
4. The menu item with the `CmdOrCtrl+B` accelerator is activated

### Actual Behavior

When the user presses `command+b` inside the `contenteditable` element, Chromium intercepts this and fires a `beforeinput` event with an input type of `formatBold`. Editors that support this (including default `contenteditable` elements) will apply the bold formatting as a result.

However, the keyboard shortcut is never handled by Electron, and the menu item is never activated.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/12joan/92d28dc884dd25103eb51e3ebb83ccee

### Additional Information

This causes problems when the intended behaviour of the menu item differs from what Chromium assumes. For example, the editor might not support bold formatting, and the developer might want `command+b` to open the user's bookmarks instead.

I wasn't able to find any way of overriding this behaviour. Calling `preventDefault` on the `beforeinput` event prevents Chromium's native behaviour of toggling bold, but Electron still isn't able to handle the keyboard shortcut itself.

In addition to `command+b`, the same thing applies to `command+i` and `command+u`, and possibly other keyboard shortcuts that I haven't encountered yet.

nodes.title: [24.1.0 regression] Unsandboxed preload is restricted by Content-Security-Policy, but only after `readyState` becomes `interactive`
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows, macOS, Other Linux

### Operating System Version

NixOS 25.11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

24.0.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

For a given preload script execution, runtime code generation via `eval` and `new Function(…)` should be consistently allowed, or consistently disallowed, depending on the Content-Security-Policy.

### Actual Behavior

As of #37756 (22.3.6, 23.2.3, 24.1.0), Electron enforces the Content-Security-Policy `script-src` for preload scripts with `sandbox: false`. However, it does so incompletely: even in the presence of a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, code generation is still allowed until `document.readyState` becomes `interactive`, at which point it becomes disallowed.

This breaks CSP detection techniques used by libraries like Zod. The first time any object schema is declared, Zod uses `try { new Function("") }` to detect whether code generation is allowed, and caches the result forever ([source](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/v4.1.5/packages/zod/src/v4/core/util.ts#L362-L375)). That should be a reasonable thing to do, but when Electron unexpectedly disallows code generation after execution has already begun, Zod starts crashing with `Uncaught EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/andersk/40e446d2932d0656821d179a8735dc72

### Additional Information

_No response_
